findings.symptom: the user-questions/request waterfall reply was a bare DshQuestionAnswer[] where the harness expects AskUserQuestionAnswer = { answers: [...] }; cordis waterfall() returns the OUTERMOST listener's value, so the roles row's array replaced the envelope and dsh-tool-ask-user threw on result.answers.map
findings.impact: every answered ask_user_question broke, including one a desktop TUI answered, because the roles row registers at boot and is an outer listener
findings.repair: DshQuestionAnswerEnvelope added; onUserQuestionRequest is envelope-in/envelope-out and forwards next()'s value UNCHANGED by identity (no re-map); the relay speaks the envelope while its parking lot stays an array; every failure path still rethrows the original error object
findings.regressionArm: a module-boundary arm runs the harness's own consumption projection (result.answers.map) and asserts it does not throw; negative control with the old mapping restored: 2 red (toBe object-vs-array, and the TypeError)
findings.contractAmended: .mpd/plans/mpd-drive-surface.md §4.1 and §4.3 (the frozen contract itself pinned the wrong shape)

findings.symptom: a panel tap resolved its option by INDEX into the LIVE parking lot, so a view held across a question change settled a question the user never saw
findings.repair: the view captures { parkedId, itemIds, raw labels } when it is built; a tap answers from that capture, and the live lot is read for one fact only (does that parked id still exist). Gone -> toast + refresh, no answer call, no index fallback
findings.regressionArm: 6 arms, all red before the repair (the new-parked-id arm received 'Answered' where it must receive 'That question is gone')

findings.symptom: the first pending question was invisible on a freshly opened panel: view() read a cache only data() fills, and the seed suppressed the refresh, so neither the callout nor the option buttons existed
findings.repair: view() is a live read of the SAME reader data() uses (readPanelState); the view-side cache was deleted
findings.regressionArm: a panel published with NO data subscription now renders the callout and one button per option

newFindings.symptom: the per-session capture is overwritten by every view build, so a tap from a STILL-DISPLAYED older view resolves against the newer capture and can settle the question the user never saw
newFindings.disposition: DECLARED BOUND, not fixed. The DSH Go tap payload carries no view identity (InvokeEvent has surface/id/action/value/locale), so with a fixed action map a client cannot tell the engine which view it tapped. The narrow repair would be a per-view revision in the action id, which the registration-time action map cannot produce. Filed as a follow-up.

bounds: No Flutter/DSH Go app in this workspace: the native panel is proven against the upstream protocol schemas, the view budget walk, the manifest gate and service doubles. A device install is the reader's check.
Route guards beyond the host fence are unit-proven against a server double (the fence answers before a bare request reaches 405/400/413), exactly as the team watchdog's routes are.
The relay's fallback behaviour is proven when nobody else answers; 'desktop plus phone' is 'the desktop wins' by construction, not by a live two-answerer run.
F1 was repaired against the installed harness SOURCES plus a module-boundary arm that replays the harness's own consumption projection — no live model round-trip was run.

The closure gate has no arm for a byte-DIFFERING file inside a required directory entry, and an invented extra file inside an artifact dsh-go is not detected (pre-existing scope of the manifest rule).

mpd-team-core's action routes reuse the team plane's existing mount seam without the watchdog's per-server WeakMap tracker: the read routes register in the same call untracked, so a second tracker would diverge.
